problem: Learning-based visual indoor navigation (VIN) work is scattered across goal types, learning paradigms (supervised vs. reinforcement learning) and generalization strategies, with no overarching report or shared theory.
motivation: VIN is a fundamental embodied AI task that underlies EQA and VLN, and classical modular map-based pipelines are brittle and need heavy manual engineering. Learning-based methods are promising but face open problems in representation, goal grounding, sample efficiency and generalization, so a holistic organization of the field is needed.
key_idea: Organize learning-based VIN work by goal description (label, image, language) and by learning paradigm (supervised representation learning vs. RL decision making), then discuss open issues: sim-to-real, SL vs. RL fairness, generalization via the learning objective, and knowledge.
insight: The survey argues that supervised learning generalizes better on homogeneous tasks but needs optimal trajectories, while RL is broadly applicable but sample-inefficient and weak at generalization. It also argues that the standard objective P(a|o;g) implicitly assumes the ground-truth map is deterministic given o and g, which encourages memorizing maps with spurious features. Remedies it proposes are data augmentation, history conditioning P(a|o;g;h), and high-level environment or knowledge representations. It is a position and survey paper with no experiments or ablations.
method: Goal taxonomy: groups VIN tasks by goal description: labels (position, room or object category, EAR), images (image-goal, object images), and natural language (EQA, VLN, REVERIE, SOON).

Representation learning view (SL): treats {(o,g,a)} from shortest or annotated paths as supervised data; covers cross-modal grounding, self-supervised auxiliary tasks, transformers, and map-like representations.
Decision-making view (RL): formulates VIN as a (PO)MDP; covers imitation pre-training, dense rewards, state representation learning, and hierarchical exploration to improve sample efficiency.

Generalization review: scene-specific layers, meta-learning, map building in new scenes, semantic and depth representations, knowledge graphs, and data augmentation (speaker-follower, environment dropout, counterfactual environments, domain randomization).

Discussion of open issues: sim-vs-real gap (e.g. sliding in Habitat), unfair SL-vs-RL comparison, learning-objective analysis via P(a|o;g)=sum_m P(a|o;g;m)P(m|o;g), and the role of commonsense knowledge.

setting.simulator: n/a (discusses AI2-THOR, House3D, Habitat, Matterport3D R2R)

numbers_note: Survey paper; no experimental results or tables.
results: No empirical results. The paper provides a taxonomy of VIN tasks and methods and identifies four future directions: sim-to-real validity, fair SL vs. RL comparison, generalization, and knowledge integration.
limitations: Short, qualitative survey with no quantitative comparison tables across methods or benchmarks.
Scope limited to indoor visual navigation as of about 2020-2021 and heavily weighted toward the authors' own works; the taxonomy is coarse.
